chunks: And Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Sakuni narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon him), from Abu Dharr (may Allah have mercy on him), who said:

I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say: 'When a person dies while traveling, do not conceal his death from his family, for it is a trust so that his wife may complete her waiting period (iddah), and his inheritance may be distributed among his family before one of them dies, causing his share to be lost.'

Completed, by the grace of Allah and His good success, what we intended regarding the commentary on the ninth part - according to our division of the book Tahdhib al-Ahkam, on the 17th of Rabi' al-Thani, in the year 1382 AH. And praise be to Allah as He deserves, and prayers upon the one after whom there is no prophet, and we ask Him for assistance to complete it, for He is the Bestower of Success. And I, the humble, Hasan al-Mawsili al-Khorasani.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on concealing the death of a traveler from their family?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq emphasizes the practical urgency of announcing death during travel to preserve the rights of heirs, specifically ensuring the widow's 'iddah' is calculated correctly and preventing the dilution of shares through subsequent deaths. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential focus on the precise administration of inheritance (mirath) and the preservation of family trusts (amanah) in dynamic circumstances.
